quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Break "red" down sound by sound. The consonant you want is either a voiced alveolar approximant or a voiced alveolar lateral approximant — remember that /r/ means you curl your tongue tip back slightly without letting it touch the roof of your mouth.
quests.explanation: The consonant in "red" is /r/, not /l/. To produce /r/, you curl your tongue tip back slightly without letting it touch the roof of your mouth; /l/ is made differently, by touching your tongue tip to the ridge behind your top teeth and letting the air flow around its sides.
quests.mouthPosition: Curl your tongue tip back slightly without letting it touch the roof of your mouth.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Say "lane" at normal speed, then again in slow motion. Isolating the consonant this way makes it much easier to tell /l/ from /r/.
quests.explanation: Here, /l/ is correct because "lane" is made by touching your tongue tip to the ridge behind your top teeth and letting the air flow around its sides. If it were /r/ instead, you'd be doing this: curling your tongue tip back slightly without letting it touch the roof of your mouth — a noticeably different articulation.
quests.mouthPosition: To produce this sound, touch your tongue tip to the ridge behind your top teeth and let the air flow around its sides.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Listen closely to "mark". For /m/, you press your lips together and let the sound hum out through your nose — like the start of "moon". Does that match what you hear?
quests.explanation: "mark" uses /m/, a voiced bilabial nasal. This contrasts with the voiced alveolar nasal /n/, heard in words like "nose", which is produced by touching your tongue tip to the ridge behind your top teeth and letting the sound hum out through your nose instead.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel it in the mouth: press your lips together and let the sound hum out through your nose.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Say "youth" slowly and isolate just the target consonant. To make /θ/, you place your tongue tip lightly behind your top teeth and blow with no voice. To make /t/, you tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with no voice. Which one are you actually doing?

Made by placing your tongue tip lightly behind your top teeth and blowing with no voice, it's a voiceless dental fricative — distinct from the voiceless alveolar plosive /t/, which instead calls for tapping your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with no voice.
